summary: Round-1 review of the new notes/smd-callback-chunk-state/jf-exact-command directory at b6628b0735a0723af5e2c9897d6b42605c943690. All required artifacts are present: scope.md, README.md, run_case.py, run_matrix.py, analyze.py, results.json, commands.json, three per-case reports, artifact-manifest.json and status.json. The harness preserves CLI semantics: run_case.py asserts the exact argv, sets sys.argv to the same ten tokens, and calls the real do_main(); the wrapped smd_callback only counts invocations and records timestamps while re-yielding the application's own events, build_batch and AreaDetectorRaw.raw are observed pass-through (the Jungfrau raw class inherits raw without override), and no filtering or computation is replaced. Protections match claims: the literal -o ./work1 skips RepoManager.save_record_at_start (RepoManager.py:320); add_shortname=False makes _short_detector_name return None instead of calling _add_detector_name -> add_document -> post (MDBWebUtils.py:794-808, 589-593); post/put/delete_cmd are patched to raise, and the only lookup path (find_docs -> request) is a GET; _get_file_info_from_db patched to {} drives the non-live on-disk scan at ds_base.py:548-551; --deploy defaults False and the nrecs==nrecs1 path writes gates via np.save only (UtilsCalib.py:743-751). The effective default of 1000 is confirmed from datasource.py:92-121,207 (_force_mfx_overrides). Source isolation is evidenced by per-case resolved paths/hashes: all .py paths resolve under the respective detached checkouts, native .so hashes are identical across cases, and the fixed overlay differs only in serial_ds, smdreader_manager plus the new callback_iterator/callback_stream modules, consistent with a Python-only fix. The negative control is specific: unfixed default records 4 chunks/4 callbacks, zero selected/raw events and UnboundLocalError on ievt, which matches UtilsJungfrauCalib.py:336/408 where ievt is first bound in the event loop and used after it. Both successful cases record 50 identical timestamps, raw shape [32,512,1024], and two gate files whose manifest SHA-256 digests are byte-identical between unfixed-10000 and fixed-default, corroborating the analyzer's exact-equality claim. README conclusions match results and state the limits (overlay not native rebuild, not Mikhail's installed build, workaround not a general fix). Findings are all low and non-blocking: an import-order dependency in the patching (JFEX-R1-001), README omissions about view_size counting transitions (JFEX-R1-002), a forward reference to round-01/ (JFEX-R1-003), post-hoc expected counts not labelled (JFAB-R1-004 reused), and the still-open application ievt bug (JFAB-R1-006 reused). JFAB-R1-005 and JFAB-R2-001 are addressed in this directory.

findings.evidence: The open_DataSource patch takes effect only because psana/psana/app/jungfrau_dark_proc.py:237 imports psana.detector.UtilsJungfrauCalibMPI lazily inside do_main(), after the patch context is entered. UtilsJungfrauCalibMPI.py:32-33 binds open_DataSource by value at import time, so if that module were ever imported earlier (e.g. by a future import in run_case.py or a changed app entry point) the callback/datasource observation would silently become a no-op while the run still completed. The committed reports confirm the patch was active in these three runs.
findings.requested_change: Non-blocking. For future reuse, add a guard such as asserting 'psana.detector.UtilsJungfrauCalibMPI' not in sys.modules before entering the patch context, or assert report['callback_calls'] > 0 or report['datasource_class'] is set after do_main() so a lost patch fails loudly; optionally note the dispatch path in README.

findings.evidence: The per-case reports list chunk view sizes 1011/1012/1013/3 (unfixed-default) and 3039 (unfixed-10000). smdreader.pyx:970-973 documents view_size as all events including transitions, so these are not L1 event counts, and README states only that results.json records observed chunk/callback counts. README also describes the entry as the serial stage-1 path without noting it is reached via the UtilsJungfrauCalibMPI dispatcher (which imports mpi4py) with MPI size 1.
